[c0]
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

authentication

### Describe the bug

When [configuring trusted certificates for mTLS](https://www.keycloak.org/server/mutual-tls), setting:
```
--https-client-auth=required
--https-trust-store-file=/path/to/file
```
also enables the client auth for the management endoint
```
--https-management-client-auth=required
```
but the truststore file setting doesn't seem to be picked up.

### Version

26.6

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Management HTTPS connection authenticated by the client certificate from the provided truststore.

### Actual behavior

SSL handshake error

### How to Reproduce?

1. Enable client auth for https: `--https-client-auth=required --https-trust-store-file=/path/to/file`.
Note: Use a different path from `conf/truststores` in order not to include the specific HTTPS truststore in the global KC trust.

2. Authenticate to KC management endpoint using the certificate provided to KC via the above truststore. --> SSL error

### Anything else?

Workaround: explicitly disable management client auth:
```
--https-management-client-auth=none
```

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @ahus1 2026-04-30T06:17:15Z:
@tkyjovsk - for the case at hand (a loadbalancer calls the probes), disabling mTLS for the management endpoint is ok, as there are no secrets on the management endpoint. 

So the new setting of `--https-management-client-auth=none` might be more than just a workaround but perfectly fine. Please continue with the blueprint and drive to completion. 

Still, something should be better aligned with mTLS for the management endpoint. Let's discuss how this could be done in this issue.
---
[c2] @vmuzikar 2026-04-30T07:24:25Z:
In the [guide](https://www.keycloak.org/server/management-interface#_tls_support), we explicitly say:
> When these options are not explicitly set, the TLS parameters are inherited from the default HTTP server.

So I agree the mTLS settings incl. the truststore should be inherited from the main HTTPS interface.
---
[c3] @shawkins 2026-04-30T12:40:43Z:
> So the new setting of --https-management-client-auth=none might be more than just a workaround but perfectly fine. Please continue with the blueprint and drive to completion.

Changing the https-management-client-auth setting is mentioned in the docs in a couple of places: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/310f61a84f137222dcd57e44a915935357318ad1/docs/guides/server/mutual-tls.adoc?plain=1#L29, https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/310f61a84f137222dcd57e44a915935357318ad1/docs/guides/observability/health.adoc#L102, and the operator docs.

> So I agree the mTLS settings incl. the truststore should be inherited from the main HTTPS interface.

Yes, if for whatever reason the user wants the management port to use mtls, then that is a reasonable expectation. Furthermore defaulting to the system truststore otherwise for the management mtls would be seen as a weakening of the expected security.
---
[c4] @vmuzikar 2026-05-25T15:10:17Z:
@shawkins Bringing this out from triage as the agreement here seems to be that management interface should inherit `https-trust-store-*` settings if not set explicitly for the management interface via `https-management-trust-store-*`.
---

title: Keycloak does an LDAP query with service account UUID when a token from a service account is used for obtaining a Requesting Party Token from a client with Authorization services
need_summary: Whether the UMA/group-policy evaluation path unnecessarily queries LDAP for a service account because it resolves the user by email/ID, as explained by the maintainer in the comments.
security_topic: unnecessary LDAP lookup during token issuance for service accounts
question_text:
Currently set up with Keycloak with the following:
- Realm with LDAP user storage.
- Service client(s) that containerized workloads authenticate with using client id and client secret
- Client that protects resources (for this set up it is kafka topics and consumer groups). The authorization uses a mix of Group policies and Client policies to grant write/read access to various topics and consumer groups.

Finding in the logs, when the service client is requesting access to the protected resource via the uma ticket flow to get a RPT token, the logs with LDAP debugging on show that and LDAP query is being done with the user storage with the UUID of the service account for the client. Example log below:

2026-04-29 14:27:07,221 DEBUG [org.keycloak.storage.ldap.idm.store.ldap.LDAPOperationManager.perf] (executor-thread-792)
LdapOperation: search
 baseDn: DC=test,DC=ad,DC=test,DC=com
 filter: (&(mail=c501b859-2de6-464b-be33-6da20f3f162c)(objectclass=person)(objectclass=organizationalPerson)(objectclass=user))
 searchScope: 2
 returningAttrs: [userPrincipalName, pwdLastSet, cn, whenChanged, whenCreated, sn, givenName, mail, userAccountControl]
 resultSize: 0
took: 131 ms

The LDAP query will not return results as this is a internal client id that does not exist in our AD. It is a wasted operation that occurs several times a minute due to reading from consumer groups via kafka.
answer_text:
The `email` scope will force iterating over any configured (LDAP) protocol mapper when resolving the username or email, hence the additional LDAP query. This happens when issuing tokens.

It is not a new behavior but something that has been there for quite some time.

I'll provide a fix to consider the same checks we have in other places to prevent unnecessary queries to user storage providers.

### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

authorization-services

### Describe the bug

Currently set up with Keycloak with the following:
- Realm with LDAP user storage.
- Service client(s) that containerized workloads authenticate with using client id and client secret
- Client that protects resources (for this set up it is kafka topics and consumer groups). The authorization uses a mix of Group policies and Client policies to grant write/read access to various topics and consumer groups.

Finding in the logs, when the service client is requesting access to the protected resource via the uma ticket flow to get a RPT token, the logs with LDAP debugging on show that and LDAP query is being done with the user storage with the UUID of the service account for the client. Example log below:

2026-04-29 14:27:07,221 DEBUG [org.keycloak.storage.ldap.idm.store.ldap.LDAPOperationManager.perf] (executor-thread-792)
LdapOperation: search

 searchScope: 2
 returningAttrs: [userPrincipalName, pwdLastSet, cn, whenChanged, whenCreated, sn, givenName, mail, userAccountControl]
 resultSize: 0
took: 131 ms

The LDAP query will not return results as this is a internal client id that does not exist in our AD. It is a wasted operation that occurs several times a minute due to reading from consumer groups via kafka.


### Version

26.6.1

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Keycloak should analyze the incoming token via the UMA ticket flow to determine if the token is coming from a service account and prevent any LDAP query of the service account.

- Realm with LDAP User storage
- Service account client
- Client with Authorization turned on and a mix of client policies and group policies protecting resources.

title: Keycloak issues tokens via implicit and hybrid flow when DPoP is enforced for the client
need_summary: Whether Keycloak’s DPoP enforcement gap for implicit and hybrid OIDC flows is a security issue, anchored by the issue’s stated bearer-token bypass and the maintainer’s acknowledgment of a security researcher report.
security_topic: DPoP enforcement bypass in implicit and hybrid OIDC flows
question_text:
When a client is configured with dpop.bound.access.tokens=true ("Require DPoP bound tokens"), Keycloak still issues front-channel bearer access tokens for OIDC:
 
 * implicit flow (response_type=token)
 * hybrid flow (response_type=code token)

The issued access tokens are active bearer tokens (token_type=Bearer) with no cnf binding claim. This bypasses the configured DPoP requirement for those response types.
answer_text:
No tokens should be issued as DPoP isn't supported for these flows.

---

Author: ahus1
Date: 2026-04-23T15:58:03Z

[c0]
### Area

oidc

### Describe the bug

When a client is configured with dpop.bound.access.tokens=true ("Require DPoP bound tokens"), Keycloak still issues front-channel bearer access tokens for OIDC:
 
 * implicit flow (response_type=token)
 * hybrid flow (response_type=code token)

The issued access tokens are active bearer tokens (token_type=Bearer) with no cnf binding claim. This bypasses the configured DPoP requirement for those response types.

### Acknowledgement

We acknowledge the security researcher Evan Hendra - Slvrqn and thank them for submitting this via our bug bounty program. 

### Version

26.5.3

### Expected behavior

No tokens should be issued as DPoP isn't supported for these flows.

Keycloak issues tokens. It then later rejects those tokens as they are not DPoP bound. 
Other resource providers are expected to reject those tokens as well assuming they are enforcing DPoP.

Try creating a new workflow

title: [OID4VCI] Replace realm options `Trusted Key IDs` and `Trusted Keys (JSON)` with the trusted-idp option on the client
need_summary: Whether reusing the same trusted key material for OID4VCI proof attestation and client attestation weakens key separation, based on the maintainer comments in the issue thread.
security_topic: trust model for attestation key validation
question_text: Moreover, the `Trusted Key IDs` is especially strange as nothing prevents potential attacker to use his own key with the pre-configured `kid`, which he himself generates and which would be the same as one of the valid "kids" from `Trusted Key IDs`, which Keycloak trusts.
answer_text: There seems to be valid reasons to have trust enforcement in the case of attestation proofs particularly permissive, given the discussion in #45693. To make this possible, I'll also pick the two-option solution. @wistefan
thread_text:
ISSUE #48414: [OID4VCI] Replace realm options `Trusted Key IDs` and `Trusted Keys (JSON)` with the trusted-idp option on the client
Author: mposolda
Date: 2026-04-23T14:10:08Z
Labels: help wanted, kind/task, area/oid4vc, release/26.7.0, team/core-protocols
State: closed

[c0]
### Description

The realm attributes `Trusted Key IDs` and `Trusted Keys (JSON)` are not so ideal for figure the attestation keys. 

As attestation is rather something, which might be different between various wallets. For example wallet lissi, which might be represented by client i.e. `lissi-client` will likely use completely different attestation keys than wallet heidi (represented by i.e. `heidi-client`) . The keys might be rather figured from identity provider (similarly like for example `CLIENT_AUTH_FEDERATED` feature is doing).

Moreover, the `Trusted Key IDs` is especially strange as nothing prevents potential attacker to use his own key with the pre-configured `kid`, which he himself generates and which would be the same as one of the valid "kids" from `Trusted Key IDs`, which Keycloak trusts.

### Action items

With the merged change for https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/48269 , the ABCA (Authentication-based client authentication) is now configured with the trusted keys provided from identity provider. The trusted-keys for OID4VCI proofs should be ideally made consistent with that approach. So as part of this PR, it would be good to:

- Remove realm options `Trusted Key IDs` and `Trusted Keys (JSON)` .

- Instead it can be good if we have option on the client, which will allow to link client with the identity-provider for trusted keys. It can be good if this option is configured on the client in the OID4VCI section. The option might be visible just if the client switch `Enable OID4VCI` is enabled. The option can be a new client configuration attribute like `OID4VCI attester trust identity providers` . It is preferred to introduce new attribute rather than re-use existing attribute `Attester trust identity providers`, which is used for ABCA as it can happen that different keys are needed to be used for ABCA and for OID4VCI proofs.

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @dominikschlosser 2026-05-25T11:39:54Z:
@mposolda Regarding the two options, i think in practice ABCA and proof key attestation will likely use the same key material. AFAIK the EUDI sandbox is doing it that way currently. But the EUDI ecosystem allows them to be separate so maybe a bit more flexibility wouldn't hurt here...

@Captain-P-Goldfish @tdiesler @IngridPuppet @thomasdarimont WDYT?
---
[c2] @IngridPuppet 2026-05-25T13:32:48Z:
There seems to be valid reasons to have trust enforcement in the case of attestation proofs particularly permissive, given the discussion in #45693. To make this possible, I'll also pick the two-option solution. @wistefan 
---
[c3] @mposolda 2026-05-26T06:37:52Z:
@dominikschlosser @IngridPuppet Thanks for the feedback! If you think we need more flexibility, two-option solution should be fine.
---
[c4] @tdiesler 2026-06-01T12:09:09Z:
We also use the same key material in OpenID conformance tests. However, in production, I would not reuse it. 
Instead, I'd prefer separate keys because they represent different trust purposes:

client_attester_keys_jwks  -> signs/verifies client attestation
key_attestation_jwks       -> signs/verifies wallet/VC key attestation

Using one key works technically if the verifier only checks signature validity and issuer/trust config, but it weakens key separation: compromise or rotation of one purpose affects the other.
---
[c5] @mposolda 2026-06-03T16:27:33Z:
@tdiesler @dominikschlosser @IngridPuppet Thanks! Updated the description of this issue to use different options based on the feedback. If anyone has a chance to contribute this change, it is welcome.
---

title: Add option to specify the CA Subject DN in the Client X.509 Authenticator
need_summary: Whether Keycloak should require and verify the CA Subject DN for X.509 client authentication, with the discussion anchored in the issue description and comments about mTLS trust-store behavior and the existing https-trust-store-file settings.
security_topic: mTLS truststore deprecation and server-level truststore necessity
question_text:
@rmartinc @vmuzikar @michalvavrik not sure what the best place is to start a discussion on this, but I wanted to see if a goal  is to eventually deprecate the https-trust-store-file-* settings again - which was the initial intent when first doing the truststore changes (undone by https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/33172). It seems like once we have support like this for both clients and users, and it's required, then the https-trust-store-file may no longer be needed.

The other rationales for keeping https-trust-store-file as undeprecated:
- it's currently reloadable, but the one created by the truststores feature won't be until at least quarkus 3.36 along with some additional refinements.
- if is there an expectation that the https-trust-store-file is being used for mTLS level access restriction, and not for authentication.
answer_text:
> but I wanted to see if a goal is to eventually deprecate the https-trust-store-file-* settings again

Not sure I follow why would we deprecate them? Unless we have e.g. a Realm Truststore, we need to keep the server level truststore for mTLS, no?
thread_text:
ISSUE #48412: Add option to specify the CA Subject DN in the Client X.509 Authenticator
Author: rmartinc
Date: 2026-04-23T13:13:55Z
Labels: area/authentication, kind/bug, priority/important, team/core-authn, release/26.7.0
State: closed

[c0]
### Description

Right now the X.509 client authenticator only allows to specify the Subject DN for the client certificate. As the trust-store (or mTLS store) is common for all the keycloak setup (same for all the realms), we can enhance this to also add the Root CA Subject DN. This way keycloak can check if the client certificate is issued by the expected CA. A very raw idea of the implementation:

* We need to re-verify the certificate in the app side and obtain the root CA (using the keycloak trust-store).
* If trusted (it should be as it was previously verified by the mTLS, but it can be more complicated when using proxies), check the Root CA has the correct and configured Subject DN.
* Check how the certificate chain is obtained in proxies. We need to obtain the full chain passed by the client.
* Document this and add a note for adding intermediate CAs if the chain is not passed by proxies.
* Add an option to disable the new working or just maintain the same old behavior if the CA DN is not specified but make it compulsory. Secure by default but old configurations maintain the old behavior. We can think about this when doing the implementation.

For the moment this issue is just for the client X.509 authentication. We will need a follow up for the user authenticator (but in that case we will need to setup a list of valid CA DNs, as maybe there are several valid CAs).

title: [CVE-2026-6856] Acceptable AAGUID policy bypass via packed self-attestation in WebAuthn registration
need_summary: Whether the packed self-attestation path in WebAuthn registration allows bypassing the acceptable AAGUID allowlist, as described in CVE-2026-6856 and the referenced CVE-2025-12150.
security_topic: AAGUID allowlist bypass in WebAuthn attestation validation
question_text: WebAuthn AAGUID policy bypass via packed self-attestation. Similar to [CVE-2025-12150](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2025-12150). When direct attestation is requested but the authenticator sends self-attestation (no x5c), the AAGUID is unverified, allowing bypass of the acceptable AAGUID allowlist.
answer_text:
The TLS trust-store can be separated to another file (https://www.keycloak.org/server/mutual-tls), but your suggestion is a very big change that probably should be managed when re-thinking the certificates per realm #33273. In general the trust-store is used for everything and there can be different usages.

This issue is just to cover the corner cases that allowed to pass a untrusted AAGUIDs.
thread_text:
ISSUE #48388: [CVE-2026-6856] Acceptable AAGUID policy bypass via packed self-attestation in WebAuthn registration
Author: ahus1
Date: 2026-04-23T07:16:43Z
Labels: priority/important, area/authentication/webauthn, kind/cve, team/core-authn, release/26.4.12, release/26.7.0, release/26.6.2
State: closed

[c0]
## Description

WebAuthn AAGUID policy bypass via packed self-attestation. Similar to [CVE-2025-12150](https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2025-12150). When direct attestation is requested but the authenticator sends self-attestation (no x5c), the AAGUID is unverified, allowing bypass of the acceptable AAGUID allowlist.

## Additional notes

By default, for a simple implementation, attestation and AAGUIDs may not be considered necessary. It's considered a high level security setting that the company uses to enforce specific authenticators or because they don't trust in users. 

## Acknowledgement

We acknowledge Pelissier, Sylvain (SICPA) for reporting this issue to the Keycloak security team.

---
*This issue was originally tracked in the private repository. Migrated by @ahus1.*

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @sylvainpelissier 2026-04-23T13:26:08Z:
There is another think I noticed while reviewing the patch,  The default truststore is the JVM's cacerts file, which contains hundreds of public commercial CAs (DigiCert, GlobalSign, Sectigo, etc.). This means every one of those CAs is implicitly trusted as a FIDO attestation CA.  Webauthn4j does validate some attestation fields like Subject-OU must be "Authenticator Attestation" or CA=false Basic Constraint, which makes a standard TLS cert unusable directly. But the architectural problem is that the trust boundary for TLS and for FIDO attestation is conflated, meaning any operator or attacker with access to add entries to the TLS truststore gains implicit power over FIDO attestation validation. In my opinion, the two trust stores should be separated.
---
[c2] @rmartinc 2026-04-23T13:38:36Z:
The TLS trust-store can be separated to another file (https://www.keycloak.org/server/mutual-tls), but your suggestion is a very big change that probably should be managed when re-thinking the certificates per realm #33273. In general the trust-store is used for everything and there can be different usages.

This issue is just to cover the corner cases that allowed to pass a untrusted AAGUIDs.
---
[c3] @sylvainpelissier 2026-04-23T13:43:45Z:
Ok maybe this is another issue but by default FIDO CA certificates have to be in a separate trust store else the AAGUID filtering may be also bypassed.
---
[c4] @ahus1 2026-04-23T15:16:59Z:
@sylvainpelissier - I think this is a good point. Please create a new issue of type "enhancement" and mention it here to link it. 
It might then be handled in a bigger context as @rmartinc mentioned, or separately when it receives a lot of community interest.

title: UMA IS_ADMIN filter breaks ticket finding
need_summary: Whether the IS_ADMIN UMA ticket filter could let cache poisoning hide or mis-handle granted tickets across resource servers, and the answer is anchored by the maintainer’s acknowledgment plus fix PR #48385.
security_topic: UMA admin filter causing cache poisoning across resource servers
question_text:
I think this new `IS_ADMIN` UMA permission ticket filter broke the caching functionality.
The MR: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/47210
I'm talking about specifically this change: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/47210/changes#diff-1e921492f31a55b4f93aaafdc92b2107801175e16b15e895108b213b9211d037R90

We have the following use case in our project as an ADMIN API: We want to retrieve all granted tickets within the system independently from their owner, requester, resource servers or anything else. This is what we do:

1. We retrieve all Resource Servers in the system

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

_No response_

### Describe the bug

Hello, 

I think this new `IS_ADMIN` UMA permission ticket filter broke the caching functionality. 
The MR: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/47210
I'm talking about specifically this change: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/47210/changes#diff-1e921492f31a55b4f93aaafdc92b2107801175e16b15e895108b213b9211d037R90

We have the following use case in our project as an ADMIN API: We want to retrieve all granted tickets within the system independently from their owner, requester, resource servers or anything else. This is what we do:

1. We retrieve all Resource Servers in the system
2. Iterate over the Resource Servers, and pull their tickets with (filters include `IS_ADMIN=true`, because we want to retrieve all tickets with the current user which is not either owner or requester):
`ticketStore.find(rs, filters, null, null)`

The above change causes Keycloak to pull **ALL tickets independently from their actual resource servers**, because it **does not** put this one: 

`predicates.add(builder.equal(root.get("resourceServer").get("id"), resourceServer.getId()));`

Then, if the first resource server is not the ticket's corresponding resource server, cache sets this ticket id as "not existing". So, when the actual resource server is queried in the next iteration, cache directly returns `null`, so we don't receive the ticket from this function call.

I think this should have been kept without touched:

```
if (resourceServer != null) {
            predicates.add(builder.equal(root.get("resourceServer").get("id"), resourceServer.getId()));
```

And, all other `IS_ADMIN` logic should be inside a separate if check.

### Version

26.5.7

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Expected behavior is:
filter contains IS_ADMIN=true

When I run ticketStore.find(rs, filter, null, null), it should **only** care about the tickets that belong to that RS, not all tickets. So that, it won't do some caching for tickets that do not belong to that RS. In other words,

This should be added regardless of IS_ADMIN filter when resource server is not null:

`predicates.add(builder.equal(root.get("resourceServer").get("id"), resourceServer.getId()));`

### Actual behavior

filter contains IS_ADMIN=true

When I run ticketStore.find(rs, filter, null, null), the `StoreFactoryCacheSession` sets a ticket as non-existing ticket in case resource servers are not matched.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create two resource servers
2. Grant a permission which belongs to first resource server (RS**1**)
3. Set filters Granted=True and IS_ADMIN=True
4. Call ticketStore.find(RS**2**, filter, null, null)
5. Call ticketStore.find(RS**1**, filter, null, null)


You won't see the granted ticket.

### Anything else?

Hi @pedroigor, thank you for quick response. 

Actually I sent you an e-mail about our general UMA use case on 9th April (assuming this is your email: psilva@redhat.com) to discuss some further points (**not** directly related to this issue).

**The related point of our use case which also touches this issue:** We want to have an admin API which can be used to see all given consents (granted tickets) within the authorization service in our application. In other words, a Keycloak admin should be able to see all given consents across all users and resource servers. Additionally, he/she should be able to revoke a certain granted consent. 

Currently, we are unable to retrieve all granted tickets with IS_ADMIN=true filter. I will provide a full script which can be used to reproduce the issue shortly.

[c4] @keycloak-github-bot 2026-04-22T20:42:23Z:
Due to the amount of issues reported by the community we are not able to prioritise resolving this issue at the moment.

If you are affected by this issue, upvote it by adding a :thumbsup: to the description. We would also welcome a contribution to fix the issue.

[c5] @erdoganege 2026-04-23T12:17:59Z:
@pedroigor sorry for the delayed response. You can find the Python script to reproduce the issue in the attachment (mostly Claude code :D). 

**PREREQUISITE:** To simulate `IS_ADMIN=true` filter, you should add this line to "GET /permission/ticket" API call ib the "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/protection/permission/PermissionTicketService.java" file:

`filters.put(PermissionTicket.FilterOption.IS_ADMIN, Boolean.TRUE.toString());`

**What does below script to (It assumes you have a running Keycloak with the above change):**
1.  Bootstrap – create a realm, two independent resource-server clients
    (RS1 and RS2), a plain requesting client, a resource-owner user (Alice),
    and a requesting user (Bob).
2.  Obtain a PAT for RS1 and register a protected resource owned by Alice.
3.  Create a UMA permission ticket for that resource.
4.  Bob exchanges the ticket for an RPT → exchange fails as expected
    (access not yet granted), and Keycloak persists a pending permission
    request that Alice can later approve.
5.  RS2 queries the pending tickets for the same resource ID. RS2 has no
    relation to this resource, so the result should be empty – but this call
    pollutes the cache under RS2's IS_ADMIN context.
6.  RS1 queries its own pending tickets for the same resource ID. This
    SHOULD return the single pending ticket from step 4, but due to the
    cache pollution in step 5 it returns an empty list  ← BUG.

**To verify correctness:** Set cache_poison to False in main(cache_poison=False) and re-run. RS1 will correctly return Bob's pending ticket.

[uma_submit_bug_final.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27010575/uma_submit_bug_final.py)

[c6] @erdoganege 2026-04-23T13:01:51Z:
I built my Keycloak with your fix, and can confirm https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/48385 fixes the issue 👍@pedroigor

title: CVE-2026-5588 Bouncy Castle Crypto Package For Java: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm vulnerability in bcpkix modules
need_summary: The thread asks whether the Bouncy Castle PKIX empty-signature validation vulnerability (GHSA-wg6q-6289-32hp / CVE-2026-5588) affects the project and notes the fix path through the Quarkus/Bouncy Castle dependency update.
security_topic: applicability of Bouncy Castle PKIX vulnerability to the project's dependency management
question_text:
Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm vulnerability in Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc. BC-JAVA bcpkix on all (pkix modules).

PKIX draft CompositeVerifier accepts empty signature sequence as valid.

This issue affects BC-JAVA: from 1.49 before 1.84.

See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wg6q-6289-32hp

Severity is moderate 6.3

Quarkus already merged version update in main: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/53700
answer_text:
@ahus1 Not really. We manage only the BC FIPS in our `pom.xml`. The affected packages like `org.bouncycastle:bcpkix-jdk18on` come from the Quarkus BOM. For the default crypto, we use the `bcprov-jdk18on`, and `bcpkix-jdk18on` - see https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/crypto/default/pom.xml#L59. 

See the Quarkus BOM that contains the BC BOM: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/bom/application/pom.xml#L3716

title: Improper status codes for user locked (both temporary/permanent)
need_summary: Whether changing the temporary-locked login error message would leak user-enumeration information, and the maintainer anchors the answer in the project’s prior change/issue #45812 plus the explicit security rationale against leaking info to attackers.
security_topic: status code and error-message handling for temporarily disabled users
question_text: We were testing it on keycloak v26.5.7, there it was 401. Can we conclude that it got fixed in 26.6.0? And can we get the error description updated to indicate a temporary disabled user?
answer_text: No, sorry, that would leak info for attackers and also means user enumeration. We have changed previously messages because of that type of reasons.

title: [ABCA] Doublecheck how to configure valid keys for client attestation authentication
need_summary: How ABCA client attestation should be configured to trust valid keys, using identity providers as the source of trusted keys via PR #48869 and the `OIDCIdentityProvider`/`DefaultTrustIdentityProvider` mechanism.
security_topic: configuration of trusted keys for client attestation authentication
question_text:
This is tracker issue for how to properly configure valid keys for ABCA. Since the initial PR https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/47962 , it uses option on the client authenticator.

This issue is to review this.

Configuration on the authenticator doesn't work as it is for whole realm, however various clients in the realm can possibly trust different keys (different client attesters). Also it is not possible with the `CLIENT_AUTH_FEDERATED`.

It can be probably good to use identity providers as a source of trusted keys.

Identity providers were originally introduced to Keycloak as "way for authenticate users" different way than by username/password and delegate authentication to other OIDC/SAML/social provider. But now they are intended to be used as more generic "trust relationship".

The feature `CLIENT_AUTH_FEDERATED` already uses identity providers as a way for check signature on the JWT provided during federated client authentication. The key is provided by underlying identity provider (could be OIDC, Spiffe or Kubernetes identity provider as of now). It seems that ABCA can likely use same mechanism?

Initially, we can maybe sufficient with the `OIDCIdentityProvider`, which means keys would be provisioned either from `jwks URL` or configured directly on the side of OIDC provider.

As a follow-up, it may be possible to introduce additional identity provider implementations (specific to OID4VCI or other use-cases).
answer_text:
This is addressed now by using identity providers as source of trusted keys.

Linked PR https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/48869 added support for clients with ABCA to have ability to configure trusted identity provider. This identity identity provider should provide the trusted keys. IDentity provider can link either using the keys from specified `OIDCIdentityProvider` (JWKS Keys) or PR introduced dedicated identity provider implementation `DefaultTrustIdentityProvider` .

title: [CVE-2026-37980] Stored XSS in select-organization.ftl - FreeMarker HTML-escape insufficient in inline JS handler
need_summary: Whether CVE-2026-37980 stored XSS in the organization selection login page is real and exploitable because HTML escaping is insufficient in an inline JavaScript onclick handler.
security_topic: stored XSS from insufficient escaping in inline JavaScript handler
question_text:
## Description

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) issue exists in the organization selection login page (`select-organization.ftl`). When an organization alias contains malicious JavaScript code, FreeMarker's `HTMLOutputFormat` escapes the value for HTML attribute context, but this escaping is insufficient when the attribute is an inline JavaScript `onclick` handler.

The browser HTML-decodes entities before passing the value to the JavaScript engine, allowing the injected script to execute. This occurs because the template uses `${organization.alias}` directly in an `onclick` attribute without JavaScript-specific escaping.
answer_text: @pedroigor the embargo has been lifted. Please provide a fix in upstream as discussed previously thanks!
thread_text:
ISSUE #48049: [CVE-2026-37980] Stored XSS in select-organization.ftl - FreeMarker HTML-escape insufficient in inline JS handler
Author: ahus1
Date: 2026-04-14T14:48:38Z
Labels: priority/important, kind/cve, team/core-iam, area/organizations, release/26.4.12, release/26.7.0, release/26.6.2
State: closed

[c0]
## Description

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) issue exists in the organization selection login page (`select-organization.ftl`). When an organization alias contains malicious JavaScript code, FreeMarker's `HTMLOutputFormat` escapes the value for HTML attribute context, but this escaping is insufficient when the attribute is an inline JavaScript `onclick` handler.

The browser HTML-decodes entities before passing the value to the JavaScript engine, allowing the injected script to execute. This occurs because the template uses `${organization.alias}` directly in an `onclick` attribute without JavaScript-specific escaping.

**Prerequisites:**
- User must have `manage-realm` or `manage-organizations` permission to create organizations with malicious aliases
- Organizations feature must be enabled in the realm

## Version Affected

26.5.5 and potentially other versions

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Log in as a user with `manage-realm` or `manage-organizations` permission
2. Create a new organization with an alias containing JavaScript code
3. Navigate to the login page where organization selection is displayed
4. Click on the organization entry
5. Observe that the JavaScript code executes in the browser

## Expected Behavior

Organization aliases should be properly escaped for JavaScript context when used in inline event handlers. The system should either:
- Use JavaScript-specific escaping for values in `onclick` handlers
- Avoid inline event handlers entirely and use event listeners instead
- Validate organization aliases to prevent JavaScript-unsafe characters

## Actual Behavior

The organization alias is only HTML-escaped, which is insufficient for inline JavaScript context. The browser decodes HTML entities before executing the JavaScript, allowing the injected code to run.

## Additional Context

This issue has been assigned CVE-2026-37980 for tracking purposes.

While this requires elevated administrative permissions (`manage-realm` or `manage-organizations`), it could be problematic in scenarios where:
- Organization names are provisioned automatically via API/automation that assumes all characters are safe
- A compromised admin account could use this to escalate access to other realms
- Multiple administrators with different trust levels manage organizations

The team is planning a comprehensive review of FreeMarker templates to identify similar context-specific escaping issues.

---

title: [CVE-2026-37977] CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflected from unverified JWT azp claim on UMA token endpoint
need_summary: Whether CVE-2026-37977 is a real cross-origin data exposure risk from CORS being set from an unverified JWT azp claim on the UMA token endpoint, anchored by the issue’s CVE and the discussion referencing the PermissionGrantType/CorsErrorResponseException behavior.
security_topic: CORS origin reflection from unverified JWT claims on token endpoint
question_text: The question is should we set CORS only when client "web origins" claim doesn't contain  "*"?
answer_text: @ValeriaEpifanova From the last comment from @stianst, we should resolve the allowed origins from the bearer token because tokens issued by Keycloak will have a specific claim with the web origins.
thread_text:
ISSUE #48036: [CVE-2026-37977] CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflected from unverified JWT azp claim on UMA token endpoint
Author: ahus1
Date: 2026-04-14T10:34:08Z
Labels: area/authorization-services, priority/important, kind/cve, team/core-iam, release/26.7.0, release/26.6.3, release/26.4.13
State: closed

[c0]
## Description

CVE-2026-37977: When using the UMA token endpoint, Keycloak sets the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` response header based on the `azp` claim from a client-provided JWT before validating the JWT signature. While the token grant itself is correctly rejected during validation, the CORS header has already been set in the response.

This allows a client to control which origin can read the error response cross-origin. The impact is limited to reading error messages - no tokens or user data are exposed.

**Prerequisites:**
- Client must be configured with `webOrigins: ["*"]` (non-default configuration)
- Only affects error responses, not successful token grants

## Version Affected

26.5.6 and potentially other versions

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Keycloak client with `webOrigins: ["*"]`
2. Create a JWT with the `azp` claim set to any origin (e.g., `https://example.com`)
3. Sign the JWT with any key (signature validation will fail later)
4. Send a POST request to `/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token` with:
   - `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:uma-ticket`
   - Include the crafted JWT
5. Inspect the response headers

## Expected Behavior

title: [OID4VCI] Self-Signed x5c Bypasses Key Attestation Validation
need_summary: Whether self-signed x5c certificates can bypass Key Attestation validation in Keycloak OID4VCI, based on the reported CWE-295 issue and the described fix that rejects self-signed certificates.
security_topic: self-signed certificate handling for key attestation validation
question_text: Would it be acceptable to still allow self-signed certs when running Keycloak in Dev-Mode? I certainly see how not allowing it at all can be cumbersome for testing/dev while it of course cannot be allowed when running in production environments.
answer_text: @dominikschlosser It seems reasonable to permit the use of self-signed certificates when running Keycloak in testing or development mode/environments .
thread_text:
ISSUE #48035: [OID4VCI] Self-Signed x5c Bypasses Key Attestation Validation
Author: ahus1
Date: 2026-04-14T10:16:26Z
Labels: kind/bug, priority/important, area/oid4vc, release/26.7.0, team/core-protocols
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

`AttestationValidatorUtil.verifierFromX5CChain()` skips PKIX certificate chain validation when `x5c[0]` is self-signed (`subject == issuer`). An attacker generates a software key, creates a self-signed cert, and forges a key attestation JWT claiming hardware-level security (VAN.5). Keycloak accepts it and issues a Verifiable Credential.

**Affected:** Keycloak <= 26.5.6 (latest stable), all versions with `oid4vc-vci` feature
**CWE:** CWE-295 (Improper Certificate Validation)

Acknowledgement: The Keycloak Security team acknowledges Trung Nguyen from CyStack Security for reporting this. 
As OID4VCI is in experimental mode, this is handled as a regular bug in upstream, and not a CVE. 
The automated reproducer is not attached to the public issue. 

## Vulnerable Code

`services/.../oid4vc/issuance/keybinding/AttestationValidatorUtil.java:332-347`

```java
// Check if this is a self-signed certificate (for test environments)
X509Certificate firstCert = certChain.get(0);
boolean isSelfSigned = firstCert.getSubjectX500Principal()
    .equals(firstCert.getIssuerX500Principal());

// Only validate the certificate chain if it's not a self-signed certificate in a test environment
if (!isSelfSigned) {
    CertPathValidator validator = CertPathValidator.getInstance("PKIX");
    PKIXParameters params = new PKIXParameters(getTrustAnchors());
    params.setRevocationEnabled(false);
    validator.validate(certPath, params);
}

PublicKey publicKey = certChain.get(0).getPublicKey();  // attacker's key trusted
```

Comment says "for test environments" but there is no runtime check. Bypass is always active.

## Execution Path

```
POST /protocol/oid4vc/credential
  AttestationProofValidator.validateProof()
    AttestationValidatorUtil.validateAttestationJwt()
      validateJwsHeader()          -- alg/typ check passes (ES256)
      verifierFromX5CChain()       -- PKIX SKIPPED for self-signed cert
      verify JWT signature         -- passes (attacker signed with own key)
      validateAttestationPayload() -- nonce/resistance checks pass
    return attested_keys           -- attacker's software JWK
  credential issued
```

No secondary defense: no SPI intercept, no realm-level trust store, no event listener.

## Confirmed

| Test | x5c cert | HTTP | Result |
|------|----------|------|--------|
| Self-signed (`subject == issuer`) | `CN=Fake WSCD` / `CN=Fake WSCD` | **200** | Credential issued |
| Non-self-signed (`subject != issuer`) | `CN=Leaf` / `CN=Fake CA` | **400** | PKIX rejects |

Tested on Keycloak **26.5.6** (latest stable) and **nightly** (2026-03-30). Both `jwt_vc_json` and `dc+sd-jwt` formats exploitable.

## Impact

Key attestation proves a credential holder's private key resides in secure hardware. This bypass allows:

- **Forge hardware attestation** -- Software key claims `iso_18045_high` (VAN.5). Server cannot distinguish from genuine hardware.
- **Clone credentials** -- Software key is exportable. Hardware-backed keys are not.
- **Identity fraud** -- In eIDAS 2.0 / EU Digital Identity Wallet, government-issued credentials (national ID, driving licence) can be obtained with forged hardware guarantees, then cloned and shared.
- **LoA bypass** -- Relying parties requiring "high" assurance accept forged credentials.

## Fix

```java
if (isSelfSigned) {
    throw new VCIssuerException(ErrorType.INVALID_PROOF,
        "Self-signed certificates are not accepted for key attestation");
}
CertPathValidator validator = CertPathValidator.getInstance("PKIX");
PKIXParameters params = new PKIXParameters(getTrustAnchors());
params.setRevocationEnabled(false);
validator.validate(certPath, params);
```



---

Would it be acceptable to still allow self-signed certs when running Keycloak in Dev-Mode? I certainly see how not allowing it at all can be cumbersome for testing/dev while it of course cannot be allowed when running in production environments.

title: [CVE-2026-4874] Server-Side Request Forgery via OIDC token endpoint manipulation
need_summary: Whether CVE-2026-4874 is exploitable via client-controlled `client_session_host` during backchannel logout, with the answer anchored by the issue description and the maintainer comment proposing validation against administrator-configured allowlisted values.
security_topic: validation of client-controlled host used in backchannel logout URL construction
question_text: CVE-2026-4874: When processing refresh token requests, Keycloak accepts a `client_session_host` parameter and stores it in the client session without validation. If a client is configured with a backchannel logout URL that includes the `application.session.host` placeholder, Keycloak will substitute this stored value when constructing the logout callback URL.
answer_text: As mentioned above the best approach is validating the 'client_session_host' value against already administrator-configured values (Root, Admin, Base and Redirect).  Will add a check before the client_session_host is added to the ClientSession note.  However, this may require some documentation for adminstrators to know they may now have to add their internal cluster subnets/specific node hostnames to the client config.  E.g.  add http://10.0.1.15/* to their Valid Redirect URIs which will then make this an allowlist for redirects and server-side backchannel requests.
thread_text:
ISSUE #47935: [CVE-2026-4874] Server-Side Request Forgery via OIDC token endpoint manipulation
Author: ahus1
Date: 2026-04-10T09:43:18Z
Labels: area/oidc, priority/important, kind/cve, team/core-authn, release/26.7.0, team/core-protocols, release/26.6.3, release/26.4.13
State: closed

[c0]
## Description

CVE-2026-4874: When processing refresh token requests, Keycloak accepts a `client_session_host` parameter and stores it in the client session without validation. If a client is configured with a backchannel logout URL that includes the `application.session.host` placeholder, Keycloak will substitute this stored value when constructing the logout callback URL.

This means that during logout operations, Keycloak may attempt to send HTTP POST requests to URLs that were provided by the client during token refresh, rather than using only administrator-configured URLs.

**Prerequisites:**
- User must have valid credentials to obtain a refresh token
- Client must be configured with `backchannel.logout.url` attribute containing the `application.session.host` placeholder
- Logout must be triggered (by admin action, user logout, or session timeout)

## Version Affected

26.5.2 and potentially other versions

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy Keycloak with a realm and create a user account
2. Create a public client with:
   - `directAccessGrantsEnabled` set to true
   - `backchannel.logout.url` attribute set to `http://${application.session.host}/callback`
3. Set up an HTTP listener on the same network as Keycloak (e.g., using Python's http.server on port 9999)
4. Obtain tokens via password grant by sending POST to `/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token` with `grant_type=password`, client_id, username, and password
5. Refresh the token with a custom host by sending POST to `/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token` with:
   - `grant_type=refresh_token`
   - The refresh_token value
   - `client_session_host=custom-listener:9999`
6. Trigger logout via admin API: POST to `/admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user_id}/logout`
7. Observe that Keycloak sends an HTTP POST request to the custom listener address

## Expected Behavior

The backchannel logout URL should only use administrator-configured values. Client-provided parameters should either be validated against allowed patterns or not be used in URL construction.

## Actual Behavior

Keycloak accepts and uses the client-provided `client_session_host` value when constructing backchannel logout URLs, allowing clients to influence which URLs Keycloak will contact during logout operations.

## Additional Context

This issue has been assigned CVE-2026-4874 for tracking purposes.

The practical impact is limited because:
- Requires valid user credentials
- Requires specific non-default client configuration
- Only affects logout callback URLs
- The feature using placeholders is being considered for deprecation

---
*This issue was originally tracked in the private repository. Migrated by @abstractj.*

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @msdaly200 2026-05-08T14:22:51Z:
As mentioned above the best approach is validating the 'client_session_host' value against already administrator-configured values (Root, Admin, Base and Redirect).  Will add a check before the client_session_host is added to the ClientSession note.  However, this may require some documentation for adminstrators to know they may now have to add their internal cluster subnets/specific node hostnames to the client config.  E.g.  add http://10.0.1.15/* to their Valid Redirect URIs which will then make this an allowlist for redirects and server-side backchannel requests.

title: FreeMarker templates allow instantiation of new objects and even running OS commands
need_summary: Whether Keycloak should disable FreeMarker `?new()` because templates can instantiate arbitrary classes and run OS commands, with the answer anchored in `DefaultFreeMarkerProvider` using `TemplateClassResolver.ALLOWS_NOTHING_RESOLVER` and the FreeMarker resolver docs.
security_topic: FreeMarker template object instantiation and command execution hardening
question_text:
The default FreeMarker configuration allows the `?new()` built-in to
instantiate arbitrary Java classes, including
`freemarker.template.utility.Execute`, which runs shell commands.

This was reported to the Keycloak security team by Kelvin Mbogo. This was later classified as a hardening issue, and not a CVE. Due to that, it is handled publicly.

Changing Freemarker template file is something only trusted users should be allowed to do, similar to changing any other file (like JavaScript sources or adding extensions).

### Version

26.2.0 and later

### Expected behavior

The functionality to instantiate new instances is not used by Keycloak's original templates, and therefore it should be disabled.
answer_text: This is just adding the `cfg.setNewBuiltinClassResolver(...)` in the [DefaultFreeMarkerProvider](https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.6.0/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/theme/freemarker/DefaultFreeMarkerProvider.java#L58). I would try first the [ALLOWS_NOTHING_RESOLVER](https://freemarker.apache.org/docs/api/freemarker/core/TemplateClassResolver.html#ALLOWS_NOTHING_RESOLVER). In all the templates the needed objects are passed and never created, so I think we can go with no new allowed. If you see an error in the tests we can try to move to the `SAFER_RESOLVER`. I don't think we can even test this, so just manual test adding something in a template and checking the new is not allowed. Probably also needed a little note in the upgrading, although I don't expect people using this.

ISSUE #47915: FreeMarker templates allow instantiation of new objects and even running OS commands
Author: ahus1
Date: 2026-04-09T19:12:28Z
Labels: kind/bug, priority/important, area/login/ui, team/core-clients, team/core-iam, team/core-authn, release/26.4.12, release/26.7.0, release/26.6.2
State: closed

[c0]
### Area

login/ui

### Describe the bug

The default FreeMarker configuration allows the `?new()` built-in to
instantiate arbitrary Java classes, including
`freemarker.template.utility.Execute`, which runs shell commands. 

This was reported to the Keycloak security team by Kelvin Mbogo. This was later classified as a hardening issue, and not a CVE. Due to that, it is handled publicly.

Changing Freemarker template file is something only trusted users should be allowed to do, similar to changing any other file (like JavaScript sources or adding extensions). 

### Version

26.2.0 and later

### Expected behavior

The functionality to instantiate new instances is not used by Keycloak's original templates, and therefore it should be disabled.

### Actual behavior

It is enabled. 

### How to Reproduce?

See internal issue.

### Anything else?

Suggested fix: One line added to DefaultFreeMarkerProvider.java after the Configuration is
constructed:

configuration.setNewBuiltinClassResolver(TemplateClassResolver.ALLOWS_NOTHING_RESOLVER);

This tells FreeMarker to reject all ?new() calls in templates, which is the
right default for a server-side template engine processing potentially
untrusted theme content.

Alternatively, SAFER_RESOLVER could be used if any legitimate theme needs
to instantiate specific approved classes, but ALLOWS_NOTHING_RESOLVER is
the safer default.

The documentation should be updated to clarify that Freemarker templates should only be changed by trusted users.

This was reported to the Keycloak security team by Kelvin Mbogo. This was later classified as a hardening issue, and not a CVE. Due to that, it is handled publicly.

Changing Freemarker template file is something only trusted users should be allowed to do, similar to changing any other file (like JavaScript sources or adding extensions). 

### Version

26.2.0 and later

### Expected behavior

The functionality to instantiate new instances is not used by Keycloak's original templates, and therefore it should be disabled.

### Actual behavior

It is enabled. 

### How to Reproduce?

See internal issue.

### Anything else?

Suggested fix: One line added to DefaultFreeMarkerProvider.java after the Configuration is
constructed:

configuration.setNewBuiltinClassResolver(TemplateClassResolver.ALLOWS_NOTHING_RESOLVER);

This tells FreeMarker to reject all ?new() calls in templates, which is the
right default for a server-side template engine processing potentially
untrusted theme content.

Alternatively, SAFER_RESOLVER could be used if any legitimate theme needs
to instantiate specific approved classes, but ALLOWS_NOTHING_RESOLVER is
the safer default.

The documentation should be updated to clarify that Freemarker templates should only be changed by trusted users.

title: Email Verify loop when mapping uppercase SAML attribute values to email
need_summary: Whether the SAML email case-mismatch bug that keeps re-adding Verify Email is fixed by PR #39885 and how to avoid it before upgrading to 26.x.
security_topic: case-sensitive email comparison causing unwanted re-verification
question_text: When a SAML identity provider has an `Attribute Importer` mapper that maps to `email`, a SAMLResponse attribute value that is identical to the user's email address (except it contains uppercase characters) will trigger a `Verify Email` required action, without any change to the user's email address.
answer_text:
Seems not a bug on latest release. This was fixed in PR #39885, targeting release was 26.x.

**What changed:** The fix ensures that a case-only difference in the email is no longer treated as a change, so the verification status is left untouched.
thread_text:
ISSUE #47740: Email Verify loop when mapping uppercase SAML attribute values to email
Author: ShawnOwczarzak
Date: 2026-04-02T18:27:38Z
Labels: area/saml, kind/bug, team/core-clients
State: closed

[c0]
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

saml

### Describe the bug

When a SAML identity provider has an `Attribute Importer` mapper that maps to `email`, a SAMLResponse attribute value that is identical to the user's email address (except it contains uppercase characters) will trigger a `Verify Email` required action, without any change to the user's email address.

Example: 
User Email: john.doe@domain.com
Incoming Attribute: John.Doe@domain.com 
Mapper Sync Override Mode: Force
Identity Provider Trust Email: Off

Result: 
- User's email remains the same
- User has a `VerifyEmail` required action added to their account




### Version

23.0.5

### Regression

- [x] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

The user does not have a `Verify Email` required action assigned to them when the email from an incoming SAML Response is the same, just with different casing.

### Actual behavior

The user is assigned the `Verify Email` required action even though their email did not change.

### How to Reproduce?

### On Keycloak Side
Setup a SAML Identity Provider.
- Trust Email = Off
- Sync Mode = Force

Setup Attribute Importer on SAML Identity Provider
- Sync Mode = Force
- Attribute Name = TestClaim
- User Attribute Name = email

Setup a user:
- Email: john.doe@domain.com
- Manually link user to IdP configuration (simplifies a bit)

### On IdP Side
Setup attributes:
- TestClaim = JOHN.DOE@domain.com

### Perform SSO Login
- User is assigned a Verify Email required action

### Anything else?

_No response_

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @bkoragan 2026-04-06T01:15:50Z:
@ShawnOwczarzak  Seems not a bug on latest release. This was fixed in PR #39885, targeting release was 26.x.

**What changed:** The fix ensures that a case-only difference in the email is no longer treated as a change, so the verification status is left untouched.

**on v23.0.5**: The SAML Attribute Importer mapper used a case-sensitive comparison to decide whether the incoming email differed from the stored one. Since Keycloak stores emails in lowercase, an uppercase value like JOHN.DOE@domain.com was treated as "different" from john.doe@domain.com. This triggered the email update path, which with Trust Email disabled — always set the email to unverified. Combined with the realm's Verify Email setting being enabled, this resulted in the user being assigned a Verify Email required action on every login, even though no actual email change occurred.

If you need this resolved before upgrading to 26.x, I would think of, these two workarounds:
1. Ensure the IdP sends email attribute values in lowercase — this avoids the case mismatch entirely or
2. Enable Trust Email on the Identity Provider — this causes the email to be marked as verified after each brokered login (only if acceptable for your security model)

**I would wait for other reviewers to confirm if any other workarounds and more insights..**
---
[c2] @ShawnOwczarzak 2026-04-06T14:16:12Z:
Thank you @bkoragan! Very helpful. 

Workaround 1 should be enough while we work to get on 26+.

Appreciate the thorough response! 🙂👍
---

title: Log Injection and Audit Forgery in OIDC Authorization Endpoint (client_id parameter)
need_summary: Whether the OIDC authorization endpoint still allows log injection and audit-forgery via unsanitized parameters, with the answer anchored by the linked PRs/issues #46743, #46740, and #46736 plus the maintainer’s note that #46743 only partially addresses it.
security_topic: log injection in OIDC authorization endpoint parameters
question_text:
### Area

oidc

### Describe the bug

A log injection vulnerability exists in the OIDC authorization endpoint where the `client_id` parameter is recorded in server logs without neutralization of ANSI escape sequences and control characters. An unauthenticated attacker can inject malicious strings that manipulate the visual output of the Keycloak audit trail. This allows for "Visual Evasion," where critical security warnings (WARN/ERROR) can be disguised as successful information events (INFO/SUCCESS) within a terminal-based monitoring environment.
answer_text:
@ahus1 Thanks for linking the issue. Just a note that https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/46743 seems to address only query parameters, but OIDC authorization endpoint is not limited to GET request. It could be sent also via POST or some other means (like `request` object or PAR).

So that PR alone is likely not sufficient for addressing this particular issue. But this one should be likely done as a follow-up to that other issue.

Similar filtering can be done probably also for token-endpoint

Implementation note: We have already some utilities to handle the [maximum size of the parameters](https://www.keycloak.org/server/all-provider-config#_openid_connect) and other stuff, so it seems that checking those validations can be handled at the same place of the codebase
thread_text: ISSUE #47681: Log Injection and Audit Forgery in OIDC Authorization Endpoint (client_id parameter) Author: Dweep018 Date: 2026-04-01T12:24:21Z Labels: area/oidc, kind/bug, priority/important, release/26.7.0, team/core-protocols State: closed [c0] ### Before reporting an issue - [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them. ### Area oidc ### Describe the bug A log injection vulnerability exists in the OIDC authorization endpoint where the `client_id` parameter is recorded in server logs without neutralization of ANSI escape sequences and control characters. An unauthenticated attacker can inject malicious strings that manipulate the visual output of the Keycloak audit trail. This allows for "Visual Evasion," where critical security warnings (WARN/ERROR) can be disguised as successful information events (INFO/SUCCESS) within a terminal-based monitoring environment. ### Version 26.5.3 ### Regression - [ ] The issue is a regression ### Expected behavior User-provided strings from the OIDC flow, specifically the `client_id`, should be sanitized before being passed to the logging subsystem. All non-printable ASCII characters (0-31) and ANSI escape sequences should be stripped or escaped to ensure the integrity of the audit log and prevent terminal-based manipulation. ### Actual behavior Keycloak reflects the raw, unsanitized `client_id` input into the `org.keycloak.events` log. 1. Visual Evasion: The logging system fails to neutralize ANSI escape codes. An attacker can inject color-coded strings (e.g., green text) into a WARN level log. This contradicts the actual system status (e.g., error="client_not_found") and can deceive security analysts during real-time monitoring. 2. Metadata Corruption: The injected payload successfully breaks the logical structure of the clientId field. By inserting a forged "Success" message directly into the metadata, the attacker compromises the readability and reliability of the audit trail. 3. Search Index Poisoning: Because the raw escape sequences (such as \u001b) are preserved in the log data, keyword-based searches in SIEM platforms (Splunk, ELK) will fail to match the affected strings, allowing malicious activity to evade automated alerting. ### How to Reproduce? 1. Setup: Start a standard Keycloak instance (Quarkus distribution) on Windows from terminal. 2. On any web browser visit `http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/account` and you will be redirected to `http://localhost:8080/realms/myrealm/protocol/openid-connect/auth` with necessary client id and parameters. 3. Input payload `fake_client%0D%0A%1b[32m[FORGED+INFO]+User+admin+logged+in+successfully%1b[0m` in the `client_id` parameter and just send the request. 4. Observe the console output. 5. Many different payloads can be tried. Sample Log Output: `2026-04-01 17:35:39,996 WARN [org.keycloak.events] (executor-thread-37) type="LOGIN_ERROR", realmId="84e00b4b-56a5-40a0-b4bf-0531c3c3951b", realmName="myrealm", clientId="fake_client [FORGED INFO] User admin logged in successfully", userId="null", ipAddress="0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1", error="client_not_found"` - `[FORGED INFO] User admin logged in successfully` appears green in terminal. POC: ### Anything else? This issue is a confirmed instance of CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs. While the use of structured logging (JSON) may prevent some physical line-breaking issues, it does not resolve the underlying problem of Semantic Poisoning. The presence of non-printable characters in the log "message" or "clientId" fields corrupts the data integrity of the system's security events. This issue exists in every realm including master realm. Suggested Remediation: - Apply a strict validation regex to the client_id parameter and implement a global log formatter that strips all ANSI and control characters before outputting to stdout or log files ## Additional details This issue is partially addressed by https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/46743 , but not fully. See https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/47681#issuecomment-4236505636 for the details on remaining stuff to be fixed. --- COMMENTS --- [c1] @Dweep018 2026-04-01T12:40:02Z: Update: Further testing confirms that the `scope` and `response_type` parameters are also vulnerable to the same. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Same as `client_id` except this time add payloads to `scope` and `response_type` one by one in different requests. 2. Payload tested: `%1B[31mTHIS_IS_RED%1B[0m` Snippet from Terminal: --- [c2] @ahus1 2026-04-02T07:51:11Z: This is similar to https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/46740 and https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/46736 and we should agree on a common filter for this one which characters we want to allow. Draft PRs exist, waiting for feedback. --- [c3] @Dweep018 2026-04-03T07:42:27Z: Thanks for linking this with the earlier issues - that aligns with my previous research which led to #46736 and #46740. A common filtering approach sounds like the right direction given the shared input handling across these parameters. Happy to review or test any of the draft PRs if that would be helpful. --- [c4] @mposolda 2026-04-13T12:52:29Z: @ahus1 Thanks for linking the issue. Just a note that https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/46743 seems to address only query parameters, but OIDC authorization endpoint is not limited to GET request. It could be sent also via POST or some other means (like `request` object or PAR). So that PR alone is likely not sufficient for addressing this particular issue. But this one should be likely done as a follow-up to that other issue. Similar filtering can be done probably also for token-endpoint Implementation note: We have already some utilities to handle the [maximum size of the parameters](https://www.keycloak.org/server/all-provider-config#_openid_connect) and other stuff, so it seems that checking those validations can be handled at the same place of the codebase --- [c5] @mposolda 2026-04-20T12:53:28Z: Triaging as important for now. It may depend on https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/46743 being addressed first. ---

title: Keycloak ships source maps for Admin UI and Account UI
need_summary: Whether serving the Admin UI and Account UI source maps in production leaks internal implementation details, with the concrete answer that production requests for .js.map files will be blocked with a 404 while preserving them in dev mode.
security_topic: source map exposure in production
question_text:
Keycloak ships source maps for the account and admin UI.

While Keycloak is Open Source software, some might customize the UIs, and then some internal code might be revealed.

This was reported by "Swornim Poudel" to the Keycloak Security team first. We're handling this publicly as this is IMHO a hardening issue, but not a security issue: The fewer information Keycloak shares, the better.
answer_text: FYI: I'm working on the filter solution so that maps can be preserved in dev mode.  If someone tries to retrieve a map file in production they will get a 404.
thread_text:
ISSUE #47545: Keycloak ships source maps for Admin UI and Account UI
Author: ahus1
Date: 2026-03-27T17:28:00Z
Labels: kind/bug, priority/important, area/account/ui, area/admin/ui, team/rh-iam, team/cloud-native, team/ui, team/core-clients, team/core-iam, team/core-shared, team/production-readiness, team/security, team/continuous-delivery, team/core-authn, release/26.7.0
State: closed

[c0]
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

account/ui

### Describe the bug

Keycloak ships source maps for the account and admin UI.

While Keycloak is Open Source software, some might customize the UIs, and then some internal code might be revealed.

This was reported by "Swornim Poudel" to the Keycloak Security team first. We're handling this publicly as this is IMHO a hardening issue, but not a security issue: The fewer information Keycloak shares, the better.

### Version

26.5.x

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Keycloak should not return source maps for the Admin UI and Account UI.

### Actual behavior

Source maps are returned.

### How to Reproduce?

Pick a JS file downloaded, and then append `.map` to it. 

### Anything else?

As this is a hardening issue, it should be marked "important". 

There might be multiple options to change this, and it would require from the teams: 

* Do not generate the source maps during build time. I assume they are not used much anyway, as there is a separate developer mode for the React UIs anyway. This could speed up the build and reduce the theme size.  
* Apply a filter to not return any `.js.map` files, at least when not in "start-dev" mode



--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @ssilvert 2026-04-17T17:47:40Z:
FYI: I'm working on the filter solution so that maps can be preserved in dev mode.  If someone tries to retrieve a map file in production they will get a 404.
---
[c2] @ahus1 2026-04-19T14:41:20Z:
> I'm working on the filter solution so that maps can be preserved in dev mode.

@ssilvert - thank you for looking into this one. Still I'm wondering: How would I use map files in the "start-dev" mode? I wouldn't expect to have the React developer console to be working just with map files? 
My impression was that I should start the React frontends in dev mode to get the full react developer experience - and that wouldn't be tied to serving any map files. 

What am I missing?  
---
[c3] @edewit 2026-04-21T06:57:30Z:
Removing source maps from production will also make it very hard to find issues as it will make stack traces useless.
---
[c4] @edewit 2026-04-21T12:37:18Z:
also is this really an issue, it will make it harder, but the source is still there you can still prettier it and read it.
---
[c5] @ssilvert 2026-04-21T17:25:08Z:
> > I'm working on the filter solution so that maps can be preserved in dev mode.
> 
> [@ssilvert](https://github.com/ssilvert) - thank you for looking into this one. Still I'm wondering: How would I use map files in the "start-dev" mode? I wouldn't expect to have the React developer console to be working just with map files? My impression was that I should start the React frontends in dev mode to get the full react developer experience - and that wouldn't be tied to serving any map files.
> 
> What am I missing?

@ahus1 If the map files are available then the browser console will show the original human-readable source instead of the minified code.  So if you are running with start-dev but not the Vite tools, you will still be able to make sense of stack traces.

I also agree with @edewit on both of his points above.  It's my impression that the main reason we need to do this so that security auditing tools won't flag a problem?

---
[c6] @ahus1 2026-04-21T19:35:05Z:
> It's my impression that the main reason we need to do this so that security auditing tools won't flag a problem?

Security is usually happier when you remove as much as possible to reduce the attack surface, and that includes publicly available information which includes the map files. Even if we don't know yet how it can be exploited, it is better to not serve them, just in case. 

There is a small possibility that people build their own themes, and then those map files might reveal information that shouldn't be revealed, so this makes it more than "just in case". A comment in the code left there by a developer could be [OSINT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_intelligence) in the hands of an attacker. 

With Claude recently revealing their source code in map files, this is now something all security researchers are looking for.  It would be a tedious task to explain to all of them why keeping the map files is ok. So it is simpler to remove them. 

So this all adds up to "please don't serve map files in production". 

PS: If you would not include the map files from the admin UI, you would save (uncompressed) 16 MB. This would reduce the image footprint for every build, download, and image spin-up. 

---
[c7] @edewit 2026-04-22T06:49:31Z:
> PS: If you would not include the map files from the admin UI, you would save (uncompressed) 16 MB. This would reduce the image footprint for every build, download, and image spin-up.

@ahus1 that is when you completely remove them (which I am in favor of), but @ssilvert suggests blocking them when loading the frontend
---
[c8] @ahus1 2026-04-22T06:53:58Z:
Thanks @edewit. I leave it to the two of you to figure out which route to choose. I'm happy as long as the map files are not available for downloading.
---

### Actual behavior

Source maps are returned.

### How to Reproduce?

Pick a JS file downloaded, and then append `.map` to it. 

### Anything else?

As this is a hardening issue, it should be marked "important". 

There might be multiple options to change this, and it would require from the teams: 

* Do not generate the source maps during build time. I assume they are not used much anyway, as there is a separate developer mode for the React UIs anyway. This could speed up the build and reduce the theme size.  
* Apply a filter to not return any `.js.map` files, at least when not in "start-dev" mode

> It's my impression that the main reason we need to do this so that security auditing tools won't flag a problem?

Security is usually happier when you remove as much as possible to reduce the attack surface, and that includes publicly available information which includes the map files. Even if we don't know yet how it can be exploited, it is better to not serve them, just in case. 

There is a small possibility that people build their own themes, and then those map files might reveal information that shouldn't be revealed, so this makes it more than "just in case". title: Token Exchange with sender constrained tokens missing cnf claim
need_summary: Whether sender-constrained tokens exchanged via token exchange should preserve the cnf confirmation claim, based on the maintainer’s guidance in the linked TokenManager code and the referenced PRs #47315 and #47571.
security_topic: sender-constrained token exchange and cnf claim handling
question_text: When configuring sender constrained tokens with `tls.client.certificate.bound.access.tokens`, it is expected that access tokens have the "cnf" confirmation claim set. However, when performing token exchange the confirmation claim is always omitted from the returned access token.
answer_text:
@ryanemerson  From 26.6, token exchange with a sender-constrained `subject_token` is not allowed in any case. It would be useful to support this only when the client that issued the `subject_token` is the same client performing the token exchange request.

The required changes are:

- In `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`, the request should be rejected only if `isSenderConstrainedToken` is true and the token azp is different from the requester client ID. Currently, it is always rejected when `isSenderConstrainedToken` is true.
- If the token is sender-constrained, we need to validate that a DPoP proof or a client certificate is present and it matches the thumbprint of the token. For DPoP, we can use `DPoPUtil.validateBinding`; for mTLS, we can use `MtlsHoKTokenUtil.verifyTokenBindingWithClientCertificate`. Similar checks can be found here:
https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/main/services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java#L531-L549
- Make sure that the thumbprint is added to the new tokens. For DPoP It should already be handled by the transient mapper. I see you adopted the same approach in the PR https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/47315, which looks good to me. But, in other flows for mtls it is added manually (see `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.checkAndBindMtlsHoKToken`).
- For the refresh token, I think it should not be bound, as standard token exchange supports only confidential clients and Keycloak DPoP feature does not bind refresh tokens for confidential clients. For mTLS, I believe it should be the same.
- Add tests for all scenarios and update the documentation. For the doc, you can extend the changes introduced in the recent PR: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/47571

title: CVE-2026-4366 Blind Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via HTTP Redirect Handling
need_summary: Whether blind SSRF via HTTP redirect handling should be fixed by disabling redirects by default, with the answer anchored by the issue’s CVE-2026-4366 and the referenced commit 8776d4bcfed4011bcfb0994955618401c89a56de.
security_topic: blind SSRF via HTTP redirect handling
question_text:
### Description

A flaw was identified in Keycloak, an identity and access management solution, where it improperly follows HTTP redirects when processing certain client configuration requests. This behavior allows an attacker to trick the server into making unintended requests to internal or restricted resources. As a result, sensitive internal services such as cloud metadata endpoints could be accessed. This issue may lead to information disclosure and enable attackers to map internal network infrastructure.

Examples include: 
* OIDC `request_uri` parameter as reported by `teaf1001`
* Dynamic client registration with `sector_identifier_uri`
answer_text:
We can disable all redirects for the HTTP client. However then we still need some backwards compatibility option and hence we should support some kind of "allow list" of the URLs, which would be allowed for redirects. It is very possible that some people even require redirects on purpose due some compatibility or other reasons and hence just disable redirects without any compatibility would be a breaking change.

My vote is to rather configure the allowed redirects at the server level, rather than realm level. It seems it is rather something, which system administrator should approve? Also server level is usually easier (realm level requires admin console changes etc...). I vote for just add an option to `HttpClientProvider` like:
```

comments.body:
### Description

A flaw was identified in Keycloak, an identity and access management solution, where it improperly follows HTTP redirects when processing certain client configuration requests. This behavior allows an attacker to trick the server into making unintended requests to internal or restricted resources. As a result, sensitive internal services such as cloud metadata endpoints could be accessed. This issue may lead to information disclosure and enable attackers to map internal network infrastructure.

Examples include: 
* OIDC `request_uri` parameter as reported by `teaf1001`
* Dynamic client registration with `sector_identifier_uri`
