title: Make sure that brokering API for retrieve-token can be called only by the confidential clients (new capabilities)
need_summary: Whether the brokering retrieve-token API is restricted to confidential clients with client authentication and audience checks, as described in issue #47256 and the linked pull request #47281.
security_topic: client authentication and audience checks for token retrieval endpoint
question_text:
### Description

As long as feature described in the #47254 is enabled, the brokering API for retrieve-token should be called only by the confidential client and it should require client authentication (currently endpoint is secured only by `Authorization: Bearer` ).

Besides client authentication, it should be checked that access token used for invocation for the token endpoint is either:
- Issued to the client, which invoked the endpoint
- The client, which invoked the endpoint is included in the `aud` claim of the access-token

Besides that, the permissions implemented in #46583 should be checked to make sure that client is permitted to retrieve external tokens of that particular IDP.
answer_text: I have looked and the current endpoint for the token retrieval is a GET. So, we probably need to move the method to POST, request client authentication and check audiences (azp and aud) in it. The current GET method can be exactly as before and it's only available if V1, the new POST is only available for V2. Nevertheless I think we can continue with https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pull/47281 and do the method separation later. That PR fixes the current broken main.

title: Missing output encoding for organization name in login error messages
need_summary: Whether reflecting the organization name in login error messages could leak user-provided content to unauthenticated callers, with the answer grounded in the maintainer comments that Keycloak sanitizes the field and that the issue is a hypothetical frontend/code-smell concern.
security_topic: whether reflecting organization names in login error messages is an actual information leak/XSS risk
question_text: The organization name is provided by the realm admin. Keycloak messages do sanitize this field. So we are speaking here about a bad admin (that can do much worse things) and hypothetical frontend that do not sanitize the organization name. Do we have an actual issue here?
answer_text:
@martin-kanis - we're talking about "A hypothetical Frontend that do not safely present the error message COMBINED with a malicious admin (which agreed can do much worse things) OR a hypothetical automatic organization self-registration where someone can choose any organization name".

The TL;DR: I'd say it is a code smell, and a good practice would be to remove the organization name from the error message. While this is a minimal technical change, would it be ok from a user's point of view to remove the organization name? It might also prevent leaking that description to an unauthenticated caller.

WDYT?

title: Make sure required actions are one-time use
need_summary: Whether all required actions were hardened to be one-time use by default, as confirmed fixed in #49112 (CVE-2026-37982) and backported to 26.4.12 and 26.6.2.
security_topic: one-time-use enforcement for required actions
question_text:
Only a few required actions are marked as one-time use:

* `UpdatePassword`
* `UpdateTotp`

We need to make sure that all required actions are marked as one-time use if they must be.
answer_text:
Yes, @pedroigor this was already fixed via #49112 (CVE-2026-37982). Now all the required actions are by default one time except if you explicitly override the method (which no one is doing right now). The issue was backported to 26.4.12 and 26.6.2 but not to 26.5 because we are not releasing more patches there.

I'm closing this as duplicate of #49112.

title: Privilege Escalation via silent group resolution fallback in Identity Provider mappers when linked to Organizations
need_summary: Whether the silent fallback from an organization-scoped IdP group mapper to a realm-level group could cause privilege escalation, and the answer cites PR #46870/#46735 and release 26.6.0.
security_topic: applicability and fix status of org-to-realm group fallback privilege escalation
question_text:
When an Identity Provider (IdP) is linked to a Keycloak Organization, the IdP group mapper (`AbstractClaimToGroupMapper`) uses `KeycloakModelUtils.getGroupForIdpMapper()` to resolve the target group during brokered authentication.

This method first searches for the group within the organization's scope. If the group is not found (e.g., it was deleted or renamed), the method **silently falls back to a realm-level group lookup using the same path**:
answer_text:
As you correctly pointed out the issue is not part of any release, this behavior was present as a work-in-progress between releases while organization groups support was being developed. It has already been tracked and resolved by #46735 (PR #46870), which landed on main and will be part of 26.6.0.

The PR eliminates the silent fallback entirely. The IdP mapper config now explicitly stores a groupType (`REALM` or `ORGANIZATION`), and the lookup is scoped strictly to the specified type — if an organization group is configured but not found, it returns null (mapper is skipped) rather than falling back to realm groups.
thread_text:
ISSUE #46997: Privilege Escalation via silent group resolution fallback in Identity Provider mappers when linked to Organizations
Author: ahus1
Date: 2026-03-09T17:04:03Z
Labels: kind/bug, team/core-iam, area/organizations
State: closed

[c0]
### Before reporting an issue

- [x] I have read and understood the above terms for submitting issues, and I understand that my issue may be closed without action if I do not follow them.

### Area

organizations

### Describe the bug

This issue was submitted by IronPhantom via our security team in #YWH-PGM40475-232. 
As this is not present in in any released version of Keycloak, this is handled publicly. 

## Vulnerability Type

Authentication Bypass / Privilege Escalation

## Affected Component(s)

- Keycloak Server — Identity Brokering (`AbstractClaimToGroupMapper`)
- `KeycloakModelUtils.getGroupForIdpMapper()` method

## Affected Version(s)

Keycloak 26.x (latest stable on main branch, commit `b7bef85f`).

## Keycloak Configuration Context (If Applicable)

- Organizations feature: **enabled** (`--features=organization`)
- At least one Organization with a linked Identity Provider
- An IdP group mapper configured with a group path that matches both an org group and a realm group

## Detailed Description

When an Identity Provider (IdP) is linked to a Keycloak Organization, the IdP group mapper (`AbstractClaimToGroupMapper`) uses `KeycloakModelUtils.getGroupForIdpMapper()` to resolve the target group during brokered authentication.

This method first searches for the group within the organization's scope. If the group is not found (e.g., it was deleted or renamed), the method **silently falls back to a realm-level group lookup using the same path**:

```java
// server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/KeycloakModelUtils.java
// Lines 1001-1026

public static GroupModel getGroupForIdpMapper(KeycloakSession session,
                                               RealmModel realm,
                                               IdentityProviderMapperModel mapperModel,
                                               BrokeredIdentityContext context) {
    String groupPath = mapperModel.getConfig().get(ConfigConstants.GROUP);
    GroupModel group = null;

    OrganizationModel organization = getOrganizationForIdpMapper(session, context.getIdpConfig());

    if (organization != null) {
        group = findGroupByPath(session, realm, organization, groupPath);
    }

    // If not found in organization (or IdP not in org context), try as realm group
    if (group == null) {
        group = findGroupByPath(session, realm, groupPath);  // <-- DANGEROUS FALLBACK
    }

    if (group == null) {
        logger.warnf("Unable to find group by path '%s' ...", groupPath, ...);
        return null;
    }
    return group;
}
```

The fallback at line `group = findGroupByPath(session, realm, groupPath)` crosses the security boundary between organization-scoped groups and realm-scoped groups. When an org group is deleted but a realm group with the same path exists, the mapper silently assigns users to the realm group instead — which typically carries higher privileges (realm-admin, manage-users, manage-clients).

The source comment itself acknowledges this behavior: `// If not found in organization (or IdP not in org context), try as realm group`. This is intentional for backward compatibility but creates a privilege escalation vector in multi-tenant deployments using Organizations.




### Version

main

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

No fallback

### Actual behavior

Fallback to a different group

### How to Reproduce?

## Steps to Reproduce (Proof of Concept - PoC)

### Prerequisites
- Keycloak instance with `--features=organization` enabled
- A realm with a group `/Admins` that has realm-admin role mappings

### Steps

1. **Create organization** "CorpA" via Admin Console or API:
```
POST /admin/realms/master/organizations
{"name": "CorpA", "enabled": true}
```

2. **Create an organization group** `/Admins` inside CorpA:
```
POST /admin/realms/master/organizations/{orgId}/groups
{"name": "Admins"}
```
This org group has org-scoped permissions only (e.g., view org members).

3. **Create an external OIDC IdP** linked to CorpA:
```
POST /admin/realms/master/identity-provider/instances
{"alias": "corp-a-idp", "providerId": "oidc", "config": {...}, "organizationId": "{orgId}"}
```

4. **Configure an IdP mapper** (Claim to Group) on this IdP:
```
POST /admin/realms/master/identity-provider/instances/corp-a-idp/mappers
{
  "name": "dept-to-admins",
  "identityProviderMapper": "oidc-advanced-group-idp-mapper",
  "config": {
    "claims": "[{\"key\":\"department\",\"value\":\"engineering\"}]",
    "group": "/Admins"
  }
}
```

5. **Verify normal behavior**: User logs in via `corp-a-idp` with `department=engineering` claim.
   - Expected: User is added to CorpA's `/Admins` group (org-scoped, low privilege)
   - Result: ✓ Correct

6. **Delete the organization group** `/Admins` from CorpA:
```
DELETE /admin/realms/master/organizations/{orgId}/groups/{orgGroupId}
```

7. **User logs in again** via `corp-a-idp` with `department=engineering` claim.
   - `getGroupForIdpMapper()` searches CorpA for `/Admins` → **not found** (deleted)
   - Falls back to `findGroupByPath(session, realm, "/Admins")`
   - Resolves to the **realm-level** `/Admins` group
   - User is added to realm `/Admins` with **realm-admin privileges**
   - Result: ✗ **PRIVILEGE ESCALATION**

### Alternative Attack: Malicious Org Admin

An org admin who cannot directly escalate their own privileges can:
1. Create org group `/Admins` matching a known realm group name
2. Configure IdP mapper pointing to `/Admins`
3. Delete the org group
4. Trigger IdP login → users promoted to realm admin


### Anything else?

## Impact

1. **Privilege Escalation**: Users authenticated through organization-linked IdPs are silently promoted from org-level groups to realm-level groups with the same name. Realm groups typically have full realm admin permissions (manage users, clients, configuration).

2. **Silent Failure**: The fallback produces no error or audit event — only a different group resolution. The admin who configured the mapper has no indication that it is now pointing to a realm group.

3. **Multi-Tenant Isolation Breach**: The Organizations feature is designed for tenant isolation. This fallback breaks isolation by allowing org-context authentication to affect realm-level resources.

4. **Attack Surface**: Triggers whenever an org group is deleted while an IdP mapper references it — admin action, API error, database inconsistency, or race condition during org restructuring.

## Recommendations

When the IdP is linked to an organization, the mapper should ONLY search within that organization's groups. The realm-level fallback should be removed for org-context lookups:

```java
if (organization != null) {
    group = findGroupByPath(session, realm, organization, groupPath);
    if (group == null) {
        // Do NOT fall back to realm groups when in org context
        logger.warnf("Group '%s' not found in organization '%s' for mapper '%s'. "
                    + "Skipping to prevent cross-boundary escalation.",
                    groupPath, organization.getName(), mapperModel.getName());
        return null;
    }
    return group;
}
// Only search realm groups when IdP is NOT linked to an organization
group = findGroupByPath(session, realm, groupPath);
```

## Supporting Material/References

- CWE-269: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html
- CVE-2026-1529: Related organization group hierarchy issue in Keycloak
- Keycloak Organizations docs: https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/#_managing_organizations
- Vulnerable code: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/b7bef85f918ba62e7c039ee5a72d7cfdc454a1d3/server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/KeycloakModelUtils.java#L1001-L1026

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @ahus1 2026-03-09T17:05:04Z:
@vramik / @pedroigor - please triage this issue. It is only related to the changes present in main, so we'll handle it publicly. 
---
[c2] @vramik 2026-03-09T18:50:19Z:
Thank you @ahus1, for reporting this and for the detailed analysis of the fallback behavior.

As you correctly pointed out the issue is not part of any release, this behavior was present as a work-in-progress between releases while organization groups support was being developed. It has already been tracked and resolved by #46735 (PR #46870), which landed on main and will be part of 26.6.0.

The PR eliminates the silent fallback entirely. The IdP mapper config now explicitly stores a groupType (`REALM` or `ORGANIZATION`), and the lookup is scoped strictly to the specified type — if an organization group is configured but not found, it returns null (mapper is skipped) rather than falling back to realm groups. Therefore I'm closing it as not-planned, please feel free to reopen if you think otherwise.

```java
    }
    return group;
}
```

The fallback at line `group = findGroupByPath(session, realm, groupPath)` crosses the security boundary between organization-scoped groups and realm-scoped groups. When an org group is deleted but a realm group with the same path exists, the mapper silently assigns users to the realm group instead — which typically carries higher privileges (realm-admin, manage-users, manage-clients).

The source comment itself acknowledges this behavior: `// If not found in organization (or IdP not in org context), try as realm group`. This is intentional for backward compatibility but creates a privilege escalation vector in multi-tenant deployments using Organizations.




### Version

main

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

No fallback

### Actual behavior

Fallback to a different group

### How to Reproduce?

## Steps to Reproduce (Proof of Concept - PoC)

### Prerequisites
- Keycloak instance with `--features=organization` enabled
- A realm with a group `/Admins` that has realm-admin role mappings

### Steps

1. **Create organization** "CorpA" via Admin Console or API:
```
POST /admin/realms/master/organizations
{"name": "CorpA", "enabled": true}
```

2. **Create an organization group** `/Admins` inside CorpA:
```
POST /admin/realms/master/organizations/{orgId}/groups
{"name": "Admins"}
```
This org group has org-scoped permissions only (e.g., view org members).

3. **Create an external OIDC IdP** linked to CorpA:
```
POST /admin/realms/master/identity-provider/instances
{"alias": "corp-a-idp", "providerId": "oidc", "config": {...}, "organizationId": "{orgId}"}
```

4. **Configure an IdP mapper** (Claim to Group) on this IdP:
```
POST /admin/realms/master/identity-provider/instances/corp-a-idp/mappers
{
  "name": "dept-to-admins",
  "identityProviderMapper": "oidc-advanced-group-idp-mapper",
  "config": {
    "claims": "[{\"key\":\"department\",\"value\":\"engineering\"}]",
    "group": "/Admins"
  }
}
```

5. **Verify normal behavior**: User logs in via `corp-a-idp` with `department=engineering` claim.
   - Expected: User is added to CorpA's `/Admins` group (org-scoped, low privilege)
   - Result: ✓ Correct

6. **Delete the organization group** `/Admins` from CorpA:
```
DELETE /admin/realms/master/organizations/{orgId}/groups/{orgGroupId}
```

7. **User logs in again** via `corp-a-idp` with `department=engineering` claim.
   - `getGroupForIdpMapper()` searches CorpA for `/Admins` → **not found** (deleted)
   - Falls back to `findGroupByPath(session, realm, "/Admins")`
   - Resolves to the **realm-level** `/Admins` group
   - User is added to realm `/Admins` with **realm-admin privileges**
   - Result: ✗ **PRIVILEGE ESCALATION**

### Alternative Attack: Malicious Org Admin

An org admin who cannot directly escalate their own privileges can:
1. Create org group `/Admins` matching a known realm group name
2. Configure IdP mapper pointing to `/Admins`
3. Delete the org group
4. Trigger IdP login → users promoted to realm admin


### Anything else?

## Impact

1. **Privilege Escalation**: Users authenticated through organization-linked IdPs are silently promoted from org-level groups to realm-level groups with the same name. Realm groups typically have full realm admin permissions (manage users, clients, configuration).

2. **Silent Failure**: The fallback produces no error or audit event — only a different group resolution. The admin who configured the mapper has no indication that it is now pointing to a realm group.

3. **Multi-Tenant Isolation Breach**: The Organizations feature is designed for tenant isolation. This fallback breaks isolation by allowing org-context authentication to affect realm-level resources.

4. **Attack Surface**: Triggers whenever an org group is deleted while an IdP mapper references it — admin action, API error, database inconsistency, or race condition during org restructuring.

## Recommendations

When the IdP is linked to an organization, the mapper should ONLY search within that organization's groups. The realm-level fallback should be removed for org-context lookups:

```java
if (organization != null) {
    group = findGroupByPath(session, realm, organization, groupPath);
    if (group == null) {
        // Do NOT fall back to realm groups when in org context
        logger.warnf("Group '%s' not found in organization '%s' for mapper '%s'. "
                    + "Skipping to prevent cross-boundary escalation.",
                    groupPath, organization.getName(), mapperModel.getName());
        return null;
    }
    return group;
}
// Only search realm groups when IdP is NOT linked to an organization
group = findGroupByPath(session, realm, groupPath);
```

## Supporting Material/References

- CWE-269: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html
- CVE-2026-1529: Related organization group hierarchy issue in Keycloak
- Keycloak Organizations docs: https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/#_managing_organizations
- Vulnerable code: https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/b7bef85f918ba62e7c039ee5a72d7cfdc454a1d3/server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/KeycloakModelUtils.java#L1001-L1026

comments.author: vramik
comments.body:
Thank you @ahus1, for reporting this and for the detailed analysis of the fallback behavior.

As you correctly pointed out the issue is not part of any release, this behavior was present as a work-in-progress between releases while organization groups support was being developed. It has already been tracked and resolved by #46735 (PR #46870), which landed on main and will be part of 26.6.0.

The PR eliminates the silent fallback entirely. The IdP mapper config now explicitly stores a groupType (`REALM` or `ORGANIZATION`), and the lookup is scoped strictly to the specified type — if an organization group is configured but not found, it returns null (mapper is skipped) rather than falling back to realm groups. Therefore I'm closing it as not-planned, please feel free to reopen if you think otherwise.

title: Security Scan Report: Object Deserialization Can Lead to Remote Code Execution
need_summary: Whether the reported unsafe Java object deserialization in TwitterIdentityProvider or KerberosSerializationUtils actually poses an RCE risk, and the maintainer’s answer points to DelegatingSerializationFilter and says the auth notes cannot be directly manipulated.
security_topic: unsafe Java object deserialization risk in Keycloak components
question_text:
During a recent SAST security scan of our **keycloak** deployment, the scanner flagged **4 findings** (2 Critical, 2 Medium) with a severity score of **94/100** related to **Unsafe Java Object Deserialization**.

Deserializing entire Java objects is dangerous because malicious actors can craft Java object streams with unintended consequences. If an attacker can control the data being deserialized, this can lead to **Remote Code Execution (RCE)** — one of the most severe vulnerability classes.

### Value Proposition

- **Prevent RCE:** Unsafe deserialization is a top OWASP vulnerability (A8:2017) that can give attackers full server control

ISSUE #46845: Security Scan Report: Object Deserialization Can Lead to Remote Code Execution
Author: AnupWellpro
Date: 2026-03-04T09:51:52Z
Labels: kind/enhancement
State: closed

[c0]
### Description

During a recent SAST security scan of our **keycloak** deployment, the scanner flagged **4 findings** (2 Critical, 2 Medium) with a severity score of **94/100** related to **Unsafe Java Object Deserialization**.

Deserializing entire Java objects is dangerous because malicious actors can craft Java object streams with unintended consequences. If an attacker can control the data being deserialized, this can lead to **Remote Code Execution (RCE)** — one of the most severe vulnerability classes.

### Value Proposition

- **Prevent RCE:** Unsafe deserialization is a top OWASP vulnerability (A8:2017) that can give attackers full server control
- **Compliance:** Eliminate Critical findings from security pipelines (SOC2, HIPAA audit readiness)
- **Reduce blast radius:** Even in test frameworks, deserialization gadget chains can be leveraged if test utilities are accidentally exposed or reused in production paths


### Goals

- [ ] Replace `ObjectInputStream` usage in `SerializationUtil.java` (both test-framework and testsuite copies) with safer alternatives — use JSON serialization (Jackson/Gson) or implement an `ObjectInputFilter` allowlist (Java 9+) to restrict deserializable classes
- [ ] Add `ObjectInputFilter` to `KerberosSerializationUtils.java` to restrict deserialization to known Kerberos credential types only
- [ ] Refactor `TwitterIdentityProvider.java` to deserialize the Base64-decoded data using JSON instead of Java object streams
- [ ] If `ObjectInputStream` must be retained, implement HMAC signature verification on the data stream before deserializing to ensure integrity and authenticity
- [ ] Add unit tests validating that crafted malicious object streams are rejected

### Non-Goals

- [ ] Rewriting Keycloak's entire serialization infrastructure — changes should be targeted to the 4 flagged locations
- [ ] Removing Kerberos support — `KerberosSerializationUtils` needs deserialization but should be hardened with filters, not removed
- [ ] Addressing test-only findings as P0 — the `SerializationUtil.java` files are in test frameworks, so while they should be fixed, they are lower operational risk than production code
- [ ] Fixing vulnerabilities outside the `keycloak` repository scope

title: Keycloak makes network requests to addresses in login certificates before verifying them
need_summary: Whether Keycloak’s certificate-revocation lookup can be abused for SSRF by making network requests to addresses embedded in an untrusted certificate, and the answer rests on the issue comment and fix direction in the thread, including the mutual-TLS trust-store guidance and the stated plan to change revocation order.
security_topic: certificate revocation check ordering and SSRF-style internal network access
question_text:
When Keycloak is configured to allow login using digital certificates (like smart cards or X.509 certificates), it can be set to check if those certificates have been canceled (revoked). It does this by looking for an address inside the certificate called a "CRL Distribution Point" and connecting to it to get a list of canceled certificates.

The issue is that Keycloak tries to connect to this address **before** it checks if the certificate was even issued by a trusted source. This allows anyone to create a fake certificate, put a private or secret internal network address inside it, and send it to Keycloak. Keycloak will then try to connect to that secret address. This allows an outsider to use the Keycloak server as a "bridge" to see into or interact with private parts of a company's network that are usually hidden.
answer_text: As we see there are several AI tools detecting this, we better change the order to do the revocation later. As commented the certificate is already validated by the mTLS before. But we are going to setup the proper order to avoid more resubmissions of the same issue.

ISSUE #46742: Keycloak makes network requests to addresses in login certificates before verifying them
Author: abstractj
Date: 2026-03-02T17:25:25Z
Labels: area/authentication, kind/bug, priority/normal, status/reopened, team/core-authn, release/26.7.0
State: closed

[c0]
## Description

When Keycloak is configured to allow login using digital certificates (like smart cards or X.509 certificates), it can be set to check if those certificates have been canceled (revoked). It does this by looking for an address inside the certificate called a "CRL Distribution Point" and connecting to it to get a list of canceled certificates.

The issue is that Keycloak tries to connect to this address **before** it checks if the certificate was even issued by a trusted source. This allows anyone to create a fake certificate, put a private or secret internal network address inside it, and send it to Keycloak. Keycloak will then try to connect to that secret address. This allows an outsider to use the Keycloak server as a "bridge" to see into or interact with private parts of a company's network that are usually hidden.

## Version affected

Keycloak 26.5.2 and earlier.

## Expected behavior

Keycloak should first verify that a certificate is signed by a trusted authority. If the certificate is not trusted, the system should stop immediately and should **not** try to connect to any web addresses listed inside that certificate.

## Actual behavior

Keycloak attempts to connect to the address listed in the certificate (using HTTP or LDAP) immediately upon receiving it, without checking if the certificate itself is valid or trusted.

## Steps to reproduce

1. **Enable Certificate Login:** Set up a Keycloak realm to use X.509 client certificate authentication and turn on the setting to check "CRL Distribution Points."
    
2. **Create a Fake Certificate:** Create a self-signed certificate. In the "CRL Distribution Point" settings of the certificate, put an address for a private internal server (for example, `http://192.168.1.50:8080/admin`).
    
3. **Log in:** Try to log in to Keycloak using this fake certificate.
    
4. **Check the logs:** You will see the Keycloak server trying to reach out to the private address you provided in the certificate, even though the certificate isn't trusted.

title: Denial of Service (DoS) via SCIM API Resource Exhaustion
need_summary: Whether the SCIM `/Users` and `/Groups` endpoints can be abused for authenticated denial of service via unbounded resource exhaustion, and the answer rests on issue #46221 plus follow-up #46684 adding pagination and a hard maxResults limit.
security_topic: pagination-based denial of service in SCIM user/group listing
question_text: The SCIM 2.0 API implementation in Keycloak is vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) through resource exhaustion (Memory and CPU). The total lack of pagination on the `/Users` (and `/Groups`) endpoints, combined with an inefficient data retrieval pattern (N+1 selects), allows an authenticated user to saturate the JVM and make the server unavailable with a single request.
answer_text: @ahus1 Issue #46221 added filtering along with pagination for this endpoint. Then, #46684 will follow up on that to add default a hard limit with the maxResults that will be applied irrespective of the filter page size. Also, unbounded requests (with no pagination) will have to respect this limit.

affected_versions: all versions including the experimental SCIM module

### Describe the bug

This was reported through out bug bounty program by "lux-cut" in YWH-PGM40475-173

## Summary 
The SCIM 2.0 API implementation in Keycloak is vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) through resource exhaustion (Memory and CPU). The total lack of pagination on the `/Users` (and `/Groups`) endpoints, combined with an inefficient data retrieval pattern (N+1 selects), allows an authenticated user to saturate the JVM and make the server unavailable with a single request.

## Vulnerability Type 
Denial of Service (DoS) - Resource Exhaustion (CWE-400)

## Affected Component(s) 
- Keycloak Server
- SCIM API Module (`scim`)

## Affected Version(s) 
- Keycloak 999.0.0-SNAPSHOT (confirmed on current development branch)
- All versions including the experimental SCIM module.

## Keycloak Configuration Context 
1. Feature enabled at startup: `--features=scim-api`.
2. SCIM enabled in the Realm: `scimEnabled: true`.
3. Attacker possessing a token with read permissions (`manage-users` or `view-users`).


### Version

main

### Regression

- [ ] The issue is a regression

### Expected behavior

Server should not crash with OOM when it retrieves all data

### Actual behavior

Server crashes with OOM

### How to Reproduce?

## Steps to Reproduce (Proof of Concept - PoC) 

1. **Start Keycloak**:

   ```bash
   ./kc.sh start-dev --features=scim-api
   ```

2. **PoC Configuration** (via script or Admin API):
   - Create a realm named `poc-realm`.
   - Enable SCIM: `curl -X PUT ... -d '{"scimEnabled": true}'`.
   - Inject 5,000 users (or more).
   - Create a client with the `manage-users` role.

3. **Triggering**:
   ```bash
   # Obtain a token for the client
   POC_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/realms/poc-realm/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
        -d "grant_type=client_credentials" -d "client_id=scim-client" -d "client_secret=scim-secret" | jq -r '.access_token')

   # Launch the vulnerable request
   time curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/scim+json" \
        http://localhost:8080/realms/poc-realm/scim/v2/Users > /dev/null
   ```

4. **Observation**:

- **Latency**: A single request for 5,000 users takes **over 1 second** (`1.023s`)
     on a local environment. In a production environment with 50,000+ users, this would le
     to request timeouts and worker thread exhaustion.
- **GC Thrashing**: Monitoring with `jstat -gcutil` during 20 concurrent requests
     showed the **Young Generation GC (YGC) count jumping from 118 to 264** in less than 1
     seconds.
- **Critical Memory Pressure**: A **Full Garbage Collection (FGC)** was triggered,
     and the Survivor space (`S1`) reached **100% saturation**. The Old Generation (`O`)
     remained consistently above **93%**, demonstrating that the JVM is struggling to mana
     the massive amount of SCIM POJOs created in memory.
- **Service Degradation**: During the attack, the server's CPU spikes due to
     intensive Garbage Collection, significantly degrading performance for all other
     legitimate authentication requests.

```bash
for i in {1..10}; do (curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/scim+json" "http://localhost:8080/realms/poc-realm/scim/v2/Users" >/dev/null &); done
```



### Anything else?

## Detailed Description 
The current implementation in `org.keycloak.scim.services.ScimResourceTypeResource` ignores standard SCIM pagination parameters (`startIndex` and `count`).

The code contains an explicit admission of this technical debt:
`// TODO: need to implement pagination and filtering, for now we just return all resources`

Technically, the impact is twofold:
1. **Memory Exhaustion**: The use of `stream.toList()` in `getAll()` forces the immediate loading of the entire user database into the JVM Heap. On a production realm, this inevitably triggers a `OutOfMemoryError`.
2. **Load Amplification (N+1)**: The `AbstractScimResourceTypeProvider` class performs a `get(id)` for each user returned by the stream to verify permissions, multiplying requests to the database or LDAP.

## Impact 
Critical for availability. A user with read rights can bring down the entire organization's SSO server, preventing any new authentication across all connected services.

## Recommendations 
- Implement pagination at the `searchForUserStream` query level (`first` and `max` parameters).
- Remove systematic list conversion (`toList()`) in favor of streaming directly to the HTTP response.
- Avoid individual `get(id)` calls within the global retrieval loop.

[c1] @ahus1 2026-03-02T09:11:45Z:
@pedroigor - this was reported in out bug bounty. As SCIM is not yet preview, this is handled publicly. This needs to be fixed before SCIM can become preview. 

I've added it here - please move it around the different milestones as you see fit. 
---
[c2] @sguilhen 2026-03-02T10:56:20Z:
@ahus1 Issue #46221 added filtering along with pagination for this endpoint. Then, #46684 will follow up on that to add default a hard limit with the maxResults that will be applied irrespective of the filter page size. Also, unbounded requests (with no pagination) will have to respect this limit.
